t.7.3.1: Then Viśravas, the son of Pulastya and the foremost of sages, within a very short time became established in austerity, just like his father.
t.7.3.2: He was truthful, virtuous and capable, devoted to the study of the Veda and pure, unattached to all pleasures, and ever intent upon dharma.
t.7.3.3: But the great sage Bharadvāja, having come to know that conduct of his, gave his own daughter Devavarṇinī to Viśravas as his wife.
t.7.3.4: Then Viśravas, the foremost of sages, having received the daughter of Bharadvāja in accordance with dharma, was filled with supreme joy.
t.7.3.5: In her that righteous-souled one begot a most wondrous offspring, endowed with valour and possessed of all the qualities of a brahmin.
t.7.3.6: When he was born, the Grandfather was overjoyed, and then, well pleased, together with the divine seers, he gave him a name.
t.7.3.7: Since he is the offspring of Viśravas and, by his likeness, is like Viśravas himself, therefore he shall be renowned by the name Vaiśravaṇa.
t.7.3.8: Then Vaiśravaṇa, of great splendour, dwelling there in the penance-grove, grew like a fire fed with oblations.
t.7.3.9: While that great-souled one dwelt in the hermitage, this resolve arose in him: "Self-restrained, I shall practise dharma, for dharma is indeed the highest goal."
t.7.3.10: He, having practised austerities for thousands of years in the great forest, took up one observance after another as each thousand years came to completion.
t.7.3.11: Subsisting on water, living on air, and likewise taking no food at all, he passed thousands of years in this way, and those thousands of years went by as though they were but a single year.
t.7.3.12: Then the greatly radiant Brahmā, pleased, went together with the hosts of gods led by Indra to the site of his hermitage and spoke these words.
t.7.3.13: I am well pleased with you, dear child, by this deed of yours, O you of excellent vows. Choose a boon, and may good fortune be yours, for I deem you worthy of a boon.
t.7.3.14: Then Vaiśravaṇa said to the Grandfather, who stood before him: "O blessed one, I would wish for the guardianship of a world-protector and the protection of wealth."
t.7.3.15: Then Brahmā, together with the hosts of gods, spoke to Vaiśravaṇa with a well-pleased heart, joyfully saying, "So be it!"
t.7.3.16: For I am intent on creating a fourth among the world-guardians, and the station held by Yama, Indra and Varuṇa is indeed what you too desire.
t.7.3.17: That is granted; go, O knower of dharma, and attain the lordship of wealth. Today you shall become the fourth alongside Yama, Indra and Varuṇa.
t.7.3.18: And accept this aerial chariot named Puṣpaka, radiant as the sun, as your vehicle, and attain equality with the thirty gods.
t.7.3.19: May all be well with you; we shall all depart just as we came. Having granted you a great boon, dear son, we have accomplished our purpose.
t.7.3.20: Then, when the gods headed by Brahmā had gone to the sky, the Lord of Wealth, bowing low out of humility, spoke these words to his father.
t.7.3.22: Therefore, O blessed one, O lord, find for us some place to dwell where there would be no harm to any living being whatsoever.
t.7.3.21: O revered one, I have obtained a boon from the Lotus-born, but that god Prajāpati did not appoint a dwelling place for me.
t.7.3.23: Thus addressed by his son, Viśravas, the foremost of sages, spoke these words: "O knower of dharma, listen, O you who understand dharma."
t.7.3.24: There is a delightful city named Laṅkā, built by Viśvakarman as a dwelling for the Rākṣasas, like Indra's Amarāvatī.
t.7.3.25: That city is indeed delightful, with arched gateways of gold and beryl; long ago it was abandoned by the Rākṣasas, who were tormented by fear of Viṣṇu, and it stands empty, all the hosts of Rākṣasas having gone down to the depths of Rasātala.
t.7.3.26: Therefore, set your own mind on dwelling there; your residence there will be free from fault, and it will be a hindrance to no one.
t.7.3.27: Having heard this most righteous speech of his father, the righteous-souled one then settled in Laṅkā on the summit of the mountain.
t.7.3.29: Then the righteous-souled son of Viśravas, lord of the Nairṛtas, dwelt there contentedly in Laṅkā, which has the ocean for its garment.
t.7.3.28: By his command, the city was soon filled, all at once, with thousands of Nairṛtas, ever joyful and delighted.
t.7.3.30: From time to time the Lord of Wealth, humble of spirit and filled with joy, went in Puṣpaka to visit his father and his mother.
t.7.3.31: Praised by the hosts of gods and gandharvas, and likewise by the siddhas together with the cāraṇas, he, enveloped in splendor and encompassed by his own might like the sun by its rays, went to the presence of his father.
